author: Kinwise NLP regression set: probe sentences written by AI review agents that the team ran as simulated judges during internal review on 2026-10-17 (an "AI-scientist" persona, probe-nlp.mts and probe2.mts; a "PM/founder" persona, probe.mjs), relabelled from eval/ANNOTATION-GUIDE.md. Not written by the NLP author, but not independent of the team, and not user or hackathon-judge testing. Not used to compute the dev or held-out scores.
format: Same as the corpora, plus: source (which simulated-judge AI agent wrote the sentence), judgeExpected (what that agent's script checked, where it had one), expectGuess (boolean fields the engine offers only as a low-confidence 'please check' guess, beyond the guide), note, and knownMiss (a documented error the engine still makes; the test checks it still misses so this file stays honest).

cases.source: simulated judge (AI agent), AI-scientist persona, r2 (probe-nlp.mts)
cases.story: I don't think I was dizzy, maybe a little light-headed when I stood.
cases.note: Hedged both ways ('I don't think I was dizzy', 'maybe a little light-headed'). Under the guide's conflict rule, no value. The simulated judge expected yes.
cases.knownMiss: The engine reads 'don't think I was dizzy' as a plain denial and 'maybe … light-headed' as a possibility, so it proposes dizziness: No. Hedged negation is not modelled (eval/NLP-ERRORS.md).
